title: Vie de sainte Thérèse écrite par elle-même
shelf_note: It is Teresa of Ávila in French, but this leaf's running head is 'LE CHEMIN' (the Way of Perfection), not the Vie, and the long-s typography is 17th-century, not 1857.
structure_note: Catalogue identity looks wrong (I7): the title says 'Vie ... écrite par elle-même', published 1857, but p.172 is headed 'Le Chemin [de la perfection]' and is set in 17th-century type (long s, 'voſtre', 'connoiſtre'). It is probably a 17th-century Arnauld d'Andilly Œuvres volume, or one containing the Chemin. Not verified beyond this leaf.

other.note: Catalogue says 1857 'Vie'; the leaf is 'Le Chemin', 17th-century typography

book_verdict: The page itself is exact and the translation is faithful, with reasonable notes. Caveat: the catalogue record (title 'Vie', date 1857) does not match a leaf headed 'Le Chemin' in 17th-century type.

title: Palladis Chymicae Arcana Detecta: Marengus (PH292)
shelf_note: An alchemical manuscript on gold 'augmentation', fluxes and cupellation; fits the title.
structure_note: 677 page records against pages_count 452, with 116 printed backsteps and 123 repeats. That suggests spread splits ('sp' image keys) were added alongside the original records, so a reader may meet the leaf twice; this needs a check. The stored page-num is 133, but the folio in the image reads 135 (or 133; the last digit is ambiguous).

title: Aristophanis Comoediae (All 11 Comedies, Greek)
shelf_note: Wasps, the trial of the dog Labes (c. ll. 910–938), 1532 Greek Aristophanes.

ocr_errors.ocr: ἐὰν δὲ μὴ λοιπὸν δὲ κεκλάγξομαι
ocr_errors.image: Ἐὰν δὲ μὴ τὸ λοιπὸν οὐ κεκλάγξομαι
ocr_errors.problem: 'τὸ' dropped and the negative 'οὐ' read as 'δὲ'

tr_errors.source: Κυ. Πρὸς ταῦτα τοῦτον κολάσατ'· οὐ γὰρ ἄν ποτε τρέφειν δύναιτ' ἂν μία λόχμη κλέπτα δύο
tr_errors.english: Dog <note>Labes</note>: Because of these things, even if you punish me, for no other way will I be able to turn, one spear cannot steal for two
tr_errors.problem: The prosecuting Dog of Kydathenaion demands that 'this one' (Labes) be punished, because one thicket cannot feed two thieves. The English makes the speaker Labes, the accused ('even if you punish me'), and the proverb becomes nonsense. Speaker and sense are reversed.

tr_errors.source: Κυνῶν ἁπάντων ἄνδρα μονοφαγίστατον
tr_errors.english: the most gluttonous of all the deaf ones
tr_errors.problem: 'dogs' rendered 'deaf ones'

tr_errors.source: τυροῦ κάκιστον ἀρτίως ἐνήρυγεν
tr_errors.english: this very wretched cheese-eater
tr_errors.problem: 'he just belched a foul whiff of cheese', the proof, is lost

tr_errors.source: Ἐμοὶ δέ γ' οὐκ ἔστ' οὐδὲ τὴν ὑδρίαν πλάσαι
tr_errors.english: And to me, he has shaped this insolence.
tr_errors.problem: 'and I can't even get my water-jar patched' is replaced by invented sense

tr_errors.source: Θερμὸς γὰρ ἀνὴρ οὐδὲν ἧττον τῆς φακῆς
tr_errors.english: For a hot man is worth nothing for lentils <note>proverbial, meaning he is useless in a pinch</note>
tr_errors.problem: means 'the fellow is as hot as the lentil soup'; the 'proverb' note is invented

tr_errors.source: νὴ τὸν Δί' ἐπιμύει γέ τοι
tr_errors.english: by Zeus, go away <note>a sudden exclamation of annoyance</note>
tr_errors.problem: 'he's winking (in assent)' is replaced, and the note is invented

tr_errors.source: ὅστις περιπλεύσας τὴν θυείαν ἐν κύκλῳ
tr_errors.english: who desires to enrich the mortar in a circle
tr_errors.problem: 'having sailed round the mortar' mistranslated

tr_errors.source: Αὐτὸς καθελεῖ· τοὺς μάρτυρας γὰρ ἐσκαλῶ
tr_errors.english: I will bring it down myself, for you are calling the witnesses
tr_errors.problem: the persons are swapped

book_verdict: The Greek is well transcribed, but the translation of the Labes trial misreads line after line: the prosecuting dog becomes the accused begging not to be punished, 'dogs' become 'deaf ones', and two invented explanatory notes are added. A reader would not get Aristophanes' scene from it.

title: Claudii Galeni Opera Omnia, Vol. 8
shelf_note: Kühn vol. 8, De locis affectis I, Greek with Latin below.
structure_note: The stored text belongs to the following printed page: the image is printed p. 67 (verso header 'ΒΙΒΛΙΟΝ Α.'), but the transcription carries p. 68's header and page-num and only its first lines. This is a one-leaf shift (I1). It should be checked on the neighbouring records.

ocr_errors.image: printed page 67, 'ΒΙΒΛΙΟΝ Α.', beginning 'οἱ δὲ μύες ἕνεκα μὲν τοῦ φυλάττεσθαι τὴν οὐσίαν αὐτῶν' / 'Musculi vero, ut substantiam suam servent' and ending 'οὕτω γοῦν καὶ κατὰ τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς' / 'Sic igitur oculis quoque saepenumero'

tr_errors.english: ...ronment happens often. For the vapors rising from the stomach certainly alter them ...
tr_errors.problem: it translates the next page's opening, not this leaf (muscles, nerves, natural and psychic organs)

pages.not_this_leaf_evidence: The stored text opens 'γίνεται πολλάκις. οἱ γὰρ ἀπὸ τῆς γαστρὸς ἀτμοὶ' / 'contingit; nam vapores a ventriculo' under a p. 68 header. The image is p. 67, which begins 'οἱ δὲ μύες ἕνεκα μὲν τοῦ φυλάττεσθαι' / 'Musculi vero, ut substantiam suam servent' and ends 'Sic igitur oculis quoque saepenumero', the words the stored text continues.

book_verdict: The wrong leaf: the reader sees p. 67 on muscles and nerves, while the text and translation are a few lines from the top of p. 68. That suggests a one-page shift (and a truncated read) in this volume, to be checked on its neighbours.

title: 近思錄·卷一~卷二 (vol 1)
shelf_note: Jinsilu (Zhu Xi), here quoting the Analects 學而 1.1 and 憲問 on learning for oneself, with commentary.

tr_errors.source: 為巳者如食之求飽衣之求溫溫飽在巳非為人也
tr_errors.english: Learning for the sake of others is like seeking satiety when eating or warmth when wearing clothes
tr_errors.problem: the commentary says learning FOR ONESELF is like eating to be full; the English assigns it to learning for others, reversing the point

tr_errors.source: 非關在我之實用故學而為巳則所得者皆實得學而為人則雖或為善亦非誠心
tr_errors.english: if it is not for others, it is within oneself. What one should be diligent about is to truly attain learning and goodness. The key lies in oneself. If one seeks practical application, then learning will penetrate the heart
tr_errors.problem: the source says learning for others has nothing to do with real use, that learning for oneself gains real attainment, and that learning for others, even when it does good, is not sincere. The English replaces this with sentences that are not in the source.

tr_errors.source: 不驟不輟
tr_errors.english: so that they do not deviate from the path
tr_errors.problem: 'neither hurried nor ceasing' mistranslated

tr_errors.source: 然人或未信則亦安其在我而巳奚慍焉盖自信之篤而無待於外所以為成德也
tr_errors.english: if people do not yet believe, one is still at peace with one's own position.
tr_errors.problem: 'why resent it? firm self-trust needing nothing outside is what makes completed virtue' is dropped

book_verdict: The transcription is exact, but the translation reverses the commentary's central contrast (learning for oneself vs for others), replaces its conclusion with sentences not in the source, and drops a clause.
